summary: One label (DSLD 232478, Tear Support with MaquiBright 60 mg) prints MaquiBright Aristotelia chilensis berry standardized extract 60 mg as its only active. PMID 31193920 randomized 74 Japanese visual display workers to MaquiBright 60 mg or placebo for 4 weeks; Schirmer's test and some symptom scores favoured MaquiBright, with no primary outcome named in the abstract. PMID 37026311 (20 patients) points the same way at an unstated amount. PMID 42351960 calls the ocular evidence the most consistent for maqui while rating overall certainty moderate to very low. The stored record's trial, PMID 26400431, tested Delphinol at 162 mg anthocyanins three times daily for oxidative stress markers, reported as change from baseline, which is not this label's preparation amount or purpose. Abstracts only.

population.description: 74 Japanese adults aged 30-60 with eye dryness, eye fatigue and at least 4 hours of visual display work daily.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, per the title; 4 weeks; 74 participants assigned equally to MaquiBright or placebo

outcomes.name: Schirmer's test lacrimal fluid production before visual display load, higher than placebo at 4 weeks (increase 6.4 mm, P = 0.005)
Eye fatigue and stiff shoulder symptoms by VAS, and bothersome ocular symptoms by DEQS, after visual display load, greater reduction than placebo

limitations: The abstract names no primary outcome, so hierarchy stays not_reported.
PubMed lists no publication type for this record; the randomized design comes from the title.
Tear break-up time, pupillary response and flicker test were measured; the abstract gives no result for them.
